scope.description: Follower main goroutine handling an AppendEntries whose first incoming entry conflicts with the stored suffix, with a faithfully implemented LogStore that returns an error from StoreLogs after DeleteRange has already succeeded (or from the deprecated peer decode after StoreLogs succeeded).
assumptions: The injected LogStore implements the LogStore interface faithfully, so DeleteRange may succeed and a later StoreLogs may return an error (for example an I/O failure).
The node is a voter in the latest configuration and stays in Follower state while the divergence persists.
excluded: LogStore implementations that cannot fail, so the error paths are unreachable
Recovery by process restart, which rebuilds lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm from the LogStore at NewRaft
The snapshot install path and any other mechanism that could re-derive the reported identity before the divergence is observed

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: skipStartup is set so the main goroutine does not run; the append handler is driven directly with a real RPC struct.
ProtocolVersion 2 is used so the deprecated peer-entry type is legal and its configuration handling runs; with protocol version < 3 the LocalID must be the network address, which the harness sets.
The deprecated entry carries an undecodable payload to make the configuration step fail after the store call succeeded; no protocol logic is altered.

plan_uncertainties: The check uses a protocol-version-2 follower and an artificially undecodable deprecated entry payload; it establishes the local responsibility, not a cluster-wide consequence.
Only the configuration-decode error return is instantiated here; the StoreLogs failure return is a separate scenario for the same claim.
grounding_unresolved: Whether any real or in-repository LogStore can return an error from StoreLogs after DeleteRange succeeded, i.e. whether the path is reachable rather than merely expressible.
Whether the divergence is confined to availability (repeatedly rejected AppendEntries and withheld votes) or can also affect a safety-relevant decision.
Whether a leader would emit a deprecated entry whose payload cannot be decoded.
